# 100.00 USD arriving as one payment, cleared by two receivable splits.
#
# A hand-written entry may clear one receivable with more than one split — two
# tranches of one wire, two lines a bookkeeper entered separately. It is still
# **one** payment: the money arrived once, and the transaction is one.
#
# Both settling splits are already on the receivable and each carries its own
# figure, 60 and 40 of the 100. Nothing has to be divided or inferred: the
# question a `payment:` block answers here is only *which* splits are this
# invoice's, which the block says outright.
#
# All three sides are USD, so the entry is USD and no rate is involved.
#
# What this fixture produces: a USD transaction with three splits, two of them
# on the receivable and neither in a lot until a payment block claims them.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
2026-02-27 * "Money in, two lines"
	guid: "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Bank:USD 100.00 USD
		guid: "6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8091223344556"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Accounts Receivable USD -60.00 USD
		guid: "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Accounts Receivable USD -40.00 USD
		guid: "8192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445566778"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
